# FIPS crypto remediation for KServe serving-stack images

## Description

Deliver KServe serving-stack images that run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no
non-validated crypto in the request path. This epic covers the audit and
remediation of all KServe-owned serving-stack images (KServe components and
the serving data plane images owned by the KServe component).

## Scope

- Audit every KServe serving-stack image to catalogue each cryptographic
  library linkage and its FIPS validation status, producing a module
  inventory (this inventory is also the input to the compliance evidence
  package).
- Replace or rebuild each non-validated crypto usage so images link only
  validated cryptographic modules in the request path.
- Rebuild the affected images in the existing build pipeline (KServe is
  already Konflux-onboarded).
- Validate the remediated images on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters:
  inference requests must succeed end-to-end exercising validated crypto
  modules only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory of all KServe serving-stack images exists, listing every
  cryptographic library linkage and its validation status.
- All KServe serving-stack images link only validated cryptographic modules
  in the request path.
- Given a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, when inference requests are served
  by the remediated images, then requests succeed end-to-end using validated
  crypto modules (measured by functional inference tests against a
  FIPS-enabled cluster).
- The remediated images build successfully in the existing build pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules — this epic delivers the requirement for the
  KServe-owned serving-stack images.

## HLR Traceability

  using validated crypto modules — this epic delivers the requirement for the
  Platform Operator images.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions in serving-stack builds

## Description

A gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which reintroduces
non-validated cryptographic usage, so the FIPS-compliant state of the model
serving stack is enforced going forward rather than eroding through
regressions.

## Scope

- Implement a regression detection check that inspects serving-stack build
  artifacts/images for non-validated crypto library usage.
- Wire the check as a gating (build-blocking) step in the CI/build pipelines
  of the serving-stack repositories, covering both the KServe and Platform
  Operator builds.
- Calibrate the check against the remediated serving-stack images: it must
  pass on the remediated images and fail on images with known non-validated
  crypto usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage,
  when the CI check runs, then the build fails (measured by injecting a known
  non-validated crypto usage into a build and observing a failed, blocked
  build).
- Given a build of the remediated serving-stack images, when the CI check
  runs, then the build passes (measured against the FIPS-remediated images
  produced by the remediation work).
- The check gates all serving-stack builds in CI — no serving-stack image can
  merge or release while reintroducing non-validated crypto usage.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

## Risks / Notes

- **Cross-team coordination**: this epic is owned by RHOAI Serving, but wiring
  the gating check into the Platform Operator CI/build pipeline touches a
  RHOAI Platform surface. The check is one logical change (one check, multiple
  pipelines), but the Platform Operator pipeline wiring requires coordination
  with RHOAI Platform before implementation — agree on the gating step's
  placement and failure handling in their build pipeline.

# FIPS compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the remediated model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and
submit it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification lab.

## Scope

- Assemble the module inventory from the crypto audits of the remediated
  serving-stack images (KServe and Platform Operator).
- Collect build attestations produced by the serving-stack build pipelines
  for the remediated images.
- Collect the FIPS validation test results from the remediated images'
  functional validation on FIPS-enabled clusters.
- Package the evidence according to the security review board's and
  certification lab's submission requirements.
- Submit the package through the security review board to the external
  certification lab, and track it through review-board triage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, build attestations,
  and test results covering all serving-stack images (KServe and Platform
  Operator).
- The build attestations included in the package are the ones produced by the
  serving-stack build pipelines for the remediated images.
- The evidence package is complete per the security review board's and
  certification lab's submission requirements.
- The evidence package is submitted through the security review board to the
  external certification lab, and the submission is tracked.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks / Notes

- The accredited certification lab's historical turnaround is six to nine
  months, and the security review board sign-off runs on its own cadence.
  Both are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering
  effort; they dominate the schedule of this epic and of the strategy. The
  epic's engineering work controls assembly and submission only — the
  certification outcome and its timing sit outside this strategy's
  requirements.

model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, reflecting the remediated, FIPS-compliant
state of the stack.

## Scope

- New documentation topic: FIPS support posture of the model serving stack
  (what is supported, and what "using validated crypto modules" means for
  the serving stack's images).
- Cluster prerequisites topic: FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster requirements
  and any constraints for the serving stack in that mode.
- Coverage of both serving deployment modes (serverless and raw deployment)
  wherever the FIPS posture or prerequisites differ between them.
- Updates to existing serving-stack documentation wherever instructions are
  affected by the FIPS posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model
  serving stack.
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled
  operation.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented FIPS
  remediation by the serving engineering team (accuracy validation), and
  review comments are addressed.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.
